description: pyMETRIC is the Western States Water Council's Python toolkit for mapping evapotranspiration with the METRIC surface-energy-balance method. It processes Landsat imagery and ancillary weather or terrain inputs into evapotranspiration estimates and supporting rasters such as albedo, vegetation indices and leaf-area index. Individual scenes can be interpolated into monthly, seasonal or annual maps. The area and image dates are selected by the user; the README documents a Harney Basin, Oregon workflow. Source is free under Apache-2.0 and the repository includes installation and step-by-step project instructions. A limitation is that the workflow depends on several outside data providers whose formats and availability can change. Its outputs also require site-aware calibration and are not direct water-use measurements. The tool can prepare irrigation-demand or basin water-balance inputs. It is a remote-sensing processing suite, not a water-network simulator. No Landsat or weather data was downloaded. Its evapotranspiration outputs are related inputs to irrigation-demand models.
